info.description: Generated from the implementation. The SRS TD-3 route registry is the canonical contract (§3.1); this document must conform to it and is never hand-edited.

code.description: The canonical application error code (TD-3.8). Extensible only by SRS revision.

message_key.description: i18n key; the client renders this.

details.description: Structured context for codes that carry it — e.g. `reason: ROOM_TIME_OVERLAP` with `conflicting_group_id`, `capacity` on CAPACITY_FULL, or `conflicting_month` on a Hijri ordering refusal. Empty object when there is nothing to add.

request_id.description: Correlates the response with the server log line.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: §4.1b routing: existing identity → session by status; pre-provisioned email match → bind identity → session by status; unknown → onboarding. Failures are REDIRECTS to /login?error=<key>, never the TD-3.8 envelope (§4.1b step 7).

302.description: Redirect by routing decision, or to /login?error=<key> on failure.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.description: One of exactly two refresh-cookie authenticated routes (TD-12, R101), with logout. The HttpOnly cookie is scoped to /api/v1/auth. Requires X-Requested-With and an Origin matching PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Rotation, the 10s predecessor grace window, and reuse detection are per TD-4.13 and §18 T1–T12.

200.description: New access token; a rotated refresh cookie unless the grace window applied.

401.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). All refusal reasons are deliberately indistinguishable.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.summary: Work as one of your own assigned roles
post.description: **SRS Revision 60.3 — the Active Role.** A person holding several roles (§2.1) chooses which one they are currently working as. **`{ role }`**; answers `{ access_token, expires_at, active_role }`. **The returned token is already NARROWED**: `roles[]` and `role_scopes[]` carry only that role's entry, so every authorization check in the platform — all 103 of them — narrows without any of them knowing this endpoint exists. A Super Admin working as `teacher` is refused by `isSuperAdmin` everywhere, including the Trash's destructive verbs. **§4.2 is unchanged**: scope still resolves per role, and the retained entry keeps its own branches, so a مؤطِّرة scoped to Marrakesh stays scoped to Marrakesh. **Decided against LIVE rows, never against the presented token** — the caller's current token may itself be narrowed, and reading it here would make the first switch a one-way door. **No logout, no new session, no refresh-cookie change**: the refresh chain records *who is signed in*, and this changes only *in what capacity*. **Not the load-bearing path**, despite appearances — the client holds the access token in memory and switching navigates by full page load, so `POST /auth/refresh` is what makes an active role persist; this endpoint exists for the immediate coded refusal and the `auth.role_switch` audit row. **This is a SAFETY mechanism, not containment** (§60.0): switching back is self-service and instant, so it cannot defend against a Super Admin who intends harm — it prevents accidents and makes testing-as-a-role truthful.

200.description: Switched; the token is narrowed to the requested role.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED when no role is given.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN with details.reason ROLE_NOT_ASSIGNED — the live rows do not carry that role for this account. 403 rather than 404: the caller is authenticated and the roles are their own, so there is nothing to hide.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.summary: Log out of the current session
post.description: The other permitted refresh-cookie authenticated route (TD-12, R101). Requires the same X-Requested-With and Origin checks as refresh, revokes the cookie's current server-side session only, and expires the HttpOnly cookie at Path=/api/v1/auth. Other devices are unaffected (TD-4.14).

204.description: Session revoked, or no current session existed. Idempotent.

401.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). Missing or invalid CSRF request context.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: Identity, roles, branch scopes, account_status and approved child links. The only endpoint (with logout) that a Pending session may call (TD-1). **R60.9: `roles[]` and `role_scopes[]` here are the LIVE assignments, read from the database rather than from the token, plus `active_role` — the one the session is currently working as, or `null` when un-narrowed.** Under an active role the token carries exactly one role, so reading it here would leave the switcher a menu of one and the person could narrow themselves and never widen again. This endpoint and authorization deliberately read different things: `/me` answers *what may this person become*, authorization answers *what is this person now*. `is_platform_owner` reports the current singleton lifecycle relationship and is distinct from roles.

200.description: Current user.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.description: **R117 unified registration.** Public and gated by the signed single-use onboarding token; email and Google subject come only from that verified token. Every new applicant supplies Arabic name parts, sex and a valid `phone`; optional French name parts are accepted only as a pair, with optional nickname/notes. `User.phone` remains nullable for honest legacy accounts and no backfill is inferred. An ordinary adult carries her requested `branch_id` and `category_id`. A هيئة التأطير request instead carries strict R115 `framing`, which is planning data and grants nothing. A `parent_child` request carries one or more children, each with her own `requested_branch_id`, `requested_category_id`, identity details and media decision; siblings may differ. Submission atomically creates the Pending guardian, verified identity, request consent, child applications and replay guard. It creates no child User, FamilyLink or child ConsentRecord: each child is independently decided under R62. No Room, Level or Group is accepted. Unknown keys are refused rather than ignored.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED or CONSENT_REQUIRED.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT on token replay; DUPLICATE if the identity exists.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

503.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). consent text version not configured (§2.3).

get.description: **§7, TD-5, BR-15, Revision 52.** Every soft-deleted record with its entity type, a label read from the snapshot, who deleted it, when, and when BR-15's 90-day window purges it. **Super Admin only** (TD-2), asserted in the service: this list spans every entity regardless of branch, so a branch-scoped Admin would see other branches' records — which no other surface allows. Filters: `entity`, `deleted_by`, `from`, `to` run in SQL; `q` narrows the page already read, because the label lives inside a JSONB snapshot under a key that differs per entity, so a SQL predicate would need one expression per type and would still miss any type added later. **`restorable` and `restore_blocked_reason` are decided by the SERVER, per entity type**, and a client must never infer them: a screen cannot know which deletions cascade, and one that guessed would offer a button that silently half-restores a person. **The `snapshot` is deliberately absent from the response** — it is the whole row as it was, including columns no screen is entitled to (a phone number, notes, `pre_provisioned_email`); this screen's question is *what was deleted, by whom, and when*, and restoration reads the snapshot server-side.

200.description: The trash page in the TD-10 envelope.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN below Super Admin.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.description: **Revision 52 — supported per entity type, and only where reinstatement is complete.** **Restorable today:** `User` under R111 (its three-day soft-delete removes no relationship row), plus `Branch`, `Category`, `Subject`, `Room`, `Exam` and `HijriMonthStart`, whose complete reinstatements are declared and tested. Revoked account credentials stay revoked after restoration. Restoring a future Exam also revalidates its supervisors under the same User locks as ordinary staffing; `STAFF_ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE` refuses the whole transaction if an account was deleted while the Exam was binned. Past staffing remains historical evidence. **Every other type is refused loudly** (`409 STATE_CONFLICT`, `reason: CASCADE_RELATIONSHIPS`, `CASCADE_CHILDREN` or `NOT_YET_SUPPORTED`) rather than silently half-restored. **A child is never restored into a deleted parent** (`PARENT_DELETED`), and `ALREADY_PURGED` answers a row BR-15 already removed. On success the record tombstone and Trash entry are removed together, while `trash.restore` preserves the event in the audit trail.

200.description: Restored; names the entity and id.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN below Super Admin.

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for an unknown trash entry.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT with reason CASCADE_RELATIONSHIPS, CASCADE_CHILDREN, NOT_YET_SUPPORTED, PARENT_DELETED, ALREADY_PURGED, NOT_DELETED or STAFF_ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

delete.description: **Revision 59.1 — the *further revision* Revision 52 required before this could exist.** Destroys the record, its **declared** cascade children and its Trash entry in ONE transaction, then writes a `trash.permanent_delete` audit row that is retained indefinitely (it is deliberately absent from the `audit.purge` allowlist). **Super Admin only** (TD-2), asserted in the service against live role rows — the `/admin/` prefix is a URL, not a boundary, and a hidden button secures nothing. Revision 52 forbade a manual *delete now* as a bypass of a retention rule; Revision 59 supersedes that because **"wait ninety days" is not an answer to a safeguarding erasure request**, and what the rule protects against is *accidental and unaccountable* destruction — which an audited, confirmed, single-role action is not. **BR-15's ninety-day window is unchanged** and remains the default path for everything nobody acts on. **Children are DECLARED per entity type, never inferred**: only rows that exist as part of the record are destroyed (an Event's four scope joins, a Schedule's staffing, an Exam's supervisors). Anything else that references it is a record in its own right, and the `Restrict` foreign key makes PostgreSQL refuse — reported as `DEPENDENTS_EXIST` with the constraint. **An `EducationalContent` purge also removes its quarantined object**, after the transaction commits: a destroyed row beside surviving bytes is an orphan, not a deletion.

204.description: Destroyed. Also the answer when only the tombstone remained (`ALREADY_PURGED` state), because removing it is exactly what was asked.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN — Super Admin only. An Admin, Teacher or Student receives this whether or not a client showed them the action.

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for an unknown trash entry.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT — DEPENDENTS_EXIST (a live row still references it, with the constraint named), NOT_DELETED (it was restored since, so the tombstone is stale), or NOT_YET_SUPPORTED / ACCOUNTABILITY_RECORD for a type with no destruction plan.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: **Super Admin only** (§5.6, TD-3.11, Revision 42), asserted against live rows per request (TD-12). Returns the **writable** settings and their current values — an explicit server-side allow-list, not every `SystemSetting`: the table also holds category default visibilities and the grading scale, which have different audiences and consequences. Each row carries `key`, `label_key`, `hint_key`, `value` and `version`. `value` is `null` when the setting has **never been configured**, which is deliberately distinct from an empty string (refused on write): for `legal.consent_text_version` a null is the state in which **no registration can be accepted at all** (§4.1a), so the screen can call it out rather than showing a blank box. Labels arrive as **i18n keys chosen by the server**, so a client cannot hold its own list and drift out of step with the allow-list.

200.description: The writable settings, configured or not.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN for anyone but a Super Admin.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

put.description: **Super Admin only** (§5.6, TD-3.11, Revision 42). Body: `{ value, version }`. **This endpoint exists because the platform was otherwise undeployable:** `legal.consent_text_version` is required before any registration is accepted (§4.1a), §15.1 deliberately does not seed it (§2.3 makes versioning the Arabic consent text an owner compliance task), and no API previously existed to set it — so a first deployment refused every applicant with no in-product remedy. **The key must be on the writable allow-list**, otherwise `404` (§20 rule 17: never a 403, which would confirm the key exists elsewhere). **The value is validated per key and may never be empty** — for the consent version, a non-blank string of 1–100 characters after trimming, because a blank version would *look* configured while reproducing the exact failure the setting prevents. **TD-15 optimistic locking:** a stale `version` is `409 VERSION_CONFLICT` rather than a silent overwrite of another Super Admin's change. **Audited as `setting.update` carrying the OLD and NEW value** (TD-8) — a row holding only the new value cannot answer *"what text was in force when this person consented"*, which is the question a compliance review asks. **A change affects FUTURE registrations only:** registration copies the version onto each `ConsentRecord` at the moment of agreement, and nothing here rewrites a stored consent, because §4.1a's requirement that each record carry the exact text agreed to is precisely what forbids restamping.

200.description: Saved; returns the setting with its incremented version.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED — empty, over-long, or wrong-typed value.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN for anyone but a Super Admin.

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for a key that is not writable through this API.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VERSION_CONFLICT.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: **R117 approval queue.** Admin or Super Admin only, with TD-12 live-account/role freshness. The union contains registrations, family links, child applications and identity reviews. Registration rows stay compact and carry an explicit `registration_details` projection for the authorized details dialog: submitted applicant names, nickname, sex, phone, verified email, notes and data-processing-consent provenance. Every `children[]` block carries that child's submitted identity/schooling details, exact requested Category and Branch, and data/media consent provenance. A mixed family has `branch`/`category` null in the compact row unless every child states the same coordinate; exact child values are never collapsed. `review_user_id` names one applicant and returns at most that still-pending registration review; absent/already-decided/deleted targets return an empty page, never a broader fallback. `type`, `branch_id`, paging and allow-listed sorting remain available when not using exact review; Branch is a reader-selected filter, never authorization scope.

200.description: Queue page; each item carries its applicants and what approving it will change.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN when the caller is no longer Active or the admin role assignment no longer exists (TD-12).

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

parameters.name: review_user_id
parameters.description: Exact applicant coordinate from registration_review_required. Returns at most the still-pending review item; a stale coordinate returns an empty page.

post.summary: Request registration for one or more children
post.description: **R117/R62.** An authenticated adult submits one or more child applications. Each child carries her own required requested Branch and Category, Arabic names, optional French-name pair/nickname, sex, optional schooling stage, explicit media decision and the request consent version/instant. Submission creates no child User or FamilyLink. Each application is independently approved or rejected; approval materializes the submitted consent and requires exact placement unless an administrator deliberately links an already-placed existing child.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED — no children, a missing name, or data-processing consent not given.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT with CONSENT_TEXT_VERSION_MISSING — §4.1a: no version, no lawful consent, no application.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: **R62.** The applications this caller submitted, and nothing else. **`internal_note` is absent from the projection** — R62.8 makes it staff-only, and a projection is where that rule holds rather than where it is merely stated. The parent sees the **bounded** `rejection_reason` only: a free-text note will eventually carry a safeguarding judgement (*"could not verify guardianship"*) that must not reach the applicant. Once a child is approved the row also carries their **reference code**, which is how a parent quotes a child without speaking a name aloud.

200.description: The caller's applications.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: **SRS Revision 65 — the personal section (§5.2 *Shared / Cross-Role*).** Role-INDEPENDENT: no role is read and none is required, because every account has a person behind it and a مؤطِّرة editing her own phone number is not acting in any capacity. **No id parameter**: the subject is the JWT `sub`, so there is nowhere for a caller to name someone else. Distinct from `GET /me`, which answers *which account is this* — roles, scopes, status, approved child links — and deliberately carries no personal detail (R63). **NEW G (2026-08-27) — the response also carries where she is placed**: `enrolments` (Category, Level, Branch and group), `circles` (§4.4c Subject circles), and `guardians`. Empty arrays are a **fact, not a gap** — a parent holds no enrolments of her own and an applicant awaiting approval holds none yet. **`guardians` carries a name and the relationship `status`, and nothing else.** Guardian email, guardian phone, account ids, identity/provider data, audit data and administrative notes are excluded **by the projection**, not by a filter applied afterwards: a guardian's contact detail is never loaded, so it is never one careless spread away from the response. A guardian field a business rule genuinely requires is to be reported and decided, never assumed. The links read are those on which the caller is the STUDENT, not those on which she is the parent — the children she is guardian of are a different relationship and a different surface.

200.description: The caller's own record, including its TD-15 `version`.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

delete.description: **R111 — every authenticated user may delete their own account** (Document Owner, 2026-08-28): Student, Teacher, Admin and Super Admin alike. **No role gate**, deliberately — the subject is the JWT `sub`, so there is nowhere for a caller to name someone else, and holding a role has never been a reason to be unable to leave. **The row is NOT removed.** Twenty-six of the thirty-five relationships referencing `"user"` must outlive the account — grades, Quran progress, enrolment, consent, safeguarding applications, guardianship, staffing history, audit — thirty-two are `RESTRICT`, and `CASCADE` is forbidden, so **deletion is the de-identification of a row that continues to exist**; nulling those columns instead would destroy the link that makes the surviving record mean anything. The soft delete sets `deleted_at` (**not** a fifth `account_status` value — TD-1's Deleted state has one source of truth so two fields cannot disagree), **revokes every live session in the same transaction** (TD-4.15's mechanism, so the account is unreachable at once rather than when the window expires), and files a `Trash` row on a **three-day** window. That window is **a second one for a single entity type and never a change to BR-15's ninety days**: they answer different questions, and Trash must show which one a row is on. Two refusals, each naming what has to change first: `409 STATE_CONFLICT` with `LAST_SUPER_ADMIN` (the platform's existing guard — Revision 22's lockout recovery needs `DATABASE_URL` and a manual seed run, a sanctioned recovery rather than something one click may produce), and `RESPONSIBILITIES_ASSIGNED` carrying a `blocked_by` breakdown of live staff duties. Those responsibilities split **by time, not by table**: past `SessionStaff`/`EventStaff`/`ExamStaff` rows are preserved history (R43.4 and R91 forbid rewriting who delivered a class) while future ones are an unfilled obligation — and a **responsible** principal on a hidden activity is the sharpest case, since R109 resolves `hidden` to *the responsible person + Super Admin*, so deleting her would leave the item visible to nobody at all.

204.description: Deleted; the session is revoked and the account is restorable for three days.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT with reason LAST_SUPER_ADMIN, or RESPONSIBILITIES_ASSIGNED carrying blocked_by.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

patch.description: **§5.2: *view/edit own basic contact info (sensitive profiling fields remain restricted)*.** Accepts **`phone` and `nickname` and nothing else**, and the exclusions are the specification rather than an oversight: **names are identity** — §1.1 composes them server-side from parts collected once, and a rename is a staff act on the §14.2 screen where it is reviewable; **`sex`** feeds §4.4b's `gender_restriction`, so self-editing it would let a person move themselves past an admission rule; **`email`** is the Google identity the account is keyed to (§4.1b); **`account_status`** is an approver's decision (TD-1); and §4.10/BR-16 safeguarding data never reaches this surface. **TD-15 optimistic locking**: the caller sends the `version` it loaded. The write reuses the existing `user.update` audit action — the same act as a staff edit by a different actor — and records the FIELDS changed, never their values (§14, no PII in logs).

200.description: The updated record.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED — a malformed phone, an over-long nickname, or a field this endpoint does not accept.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VERSION_CONFLICT — the row changed since it was loaded (TD-15).

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: **SRS Revision 63 — the Student Dashboard read (§5.3, R62.10).** `me` here is the **acting student, not the account**: `GET /me` answers *which account is this*, and for a parent the two name different people. The subject is resolved by the `X-Active-Child-ID` middleware (§4.3) — an approved `FamilyLink` matching **both** the JWT parent and the header child, or the caller themselves when they hold the Student role and send no header. **There is no `{id}` in the path, and that is the security property**: TD-12 forbids trusting a student identifier from the request, so there is nowhere here for a caller to name a different student. The response carries **exactly R62.10's five fields** — name, reference code, Category, Level, branch — and nothing else: no sex, no schooling stage, no French name, no consent state, no account status, no dates, because every field added to a screen a parent looks at publishes personal data to one more surface for no stated purpose. `enrollments` is a **list** because `Enrollment` is unique on `(student_id, level_id)` and a student may hold one per Level; a singular field would have to choose one and silently discard the rest. `reference_code` is `null` for adult students and for accounts predating R62. **Reads are deliberately not audited**, unlike `StudentSocialProfile` (§4.10, R28) — a student or their approved parent reading a name and a Level is ordinary use.

200.description: The identity block; `{ id, name_arabic, reference_code, enrollments[] }`.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED — a Parent-only caller sent no `X-Active-Child-ID`, so the request names no student. Staff receive this too: they reach a student record through §14.2 and TD-2, a different authorization path.

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for a header resolving to no approved (parent, child) link — pending, revoked, deleted, nonexistent, or another parent's child, with no distinction between them (§4.3, §20 rule 17).

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.summary: Existing accounts this child might already have
get.description: **R62.3 — proposals, never a merge.** There is **no natural key for a child**: no national identifier and, by decision, no date of birth. Matching on names alone would eventually attach a child to the wrong family, which is a safeguarding failure no audit row undoes — so the platform **proposes** and an administrator decides. Each candidate carries **the parent it is already linked to and its reference code**, which is what lets an administrator tell two same-named children apart without the platform holding a precise identifier for either. Candidates are **minors only** — accounts with no active login — because an adult consents for themselves.

200.description: Candidate accounts.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN — approver roles only.

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for an unknown application.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.description: **SRS Revision 62.2 — TD-4.2 narrowed from the bundle to a single child.** Approving creates or links that child, creates the `FamilyLink(approved)`, materialises the consent records **with the submission's values**, grants the `parent` role **if the parent does not already hold it**, and audits — all in one transaction, leaving every sibling untouched. **The parent's own application is decided separately and is never inferred from the children's outcomes.** Rejection creates **nothing** and requires a **bounded** `rejection_reason`; the optional `internal_note` is staff-only and is never returned to a parent. `match_existing_user_id` links an account the administrator chose — refused with `ACCOUNT_HAS_LOGIN` if it has its own login, because an adult consents for themselves and linking would hand a third party their record. `administrative_group_id` places the child through the **existing** enrolment service, so approval and the roster screen place students by the same rules. **`schooling_stage` informs placement and gates nothing** (R62.7): no logic here reads it to choose, validate or refuse a group — a student older than the usual high-school age still belongs in اليافعون if she is still in high school. TD-12 freshness applies, and TD-15.3 makes a double decision first-wins.

200.description: Decided; `{ child_user_id, parent_role_granted }`.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED — a rejection with no bounded reason.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN — approver roles only, re-read from live rows (TD-12).

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for an unknown application or account.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT — ALREADY_DECIDED (TD-15.3 first-wins) or ACCOUNT_HAS_LOGIN.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.description: **R117 approval semantics.** Adult-beneficiary approval requires complete placement and atomically activates, marks beneficiary, grants structural Student authority and creates the Enrollment(s). A parent/child registration id activates only the guardian: it creates no beneficiary flag, Student assignment or Enrollment for the parent, and leaves every child application for its own independent decision. Staff requests grant only assignments explicitly approved by an authorized caller. Any validation/authorization/notification failure rolls back the whole decision.

200.description: Approved; reports the item type and how many accounts were activated.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN (TD-12 freshness or TD-2 role).

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT when the item was already decided.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

post.description: **R117/R62.** Rejects the exact adult/guardian registration and requires a bounded reason. It does not infer a decision for any child application; each sibling remains independently approvable or rejectable. Rejection and its session/audit effects are one transaction.

200.description: Rejected; the reason is stored on the decision and in the audit row.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED when the reason is missing or too long.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8).

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8).

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT when the item was already decided.

500.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). INTERNAL — unexpected server fault; details are never leaked to the client.

get.description: TD-3.9 (Revision 35) — the §5.1 landing-page branch list, **anonymous**. Returns **only** `id`, `name`, `address`, `phone`, `email`, `opening_hours_ar`, `google_maps_url` and `display_order`; `version`, `operational_start_date`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at` and `deleted_by` are **never** exposed. The projection is an explicit `select`, not a filtered read, so a column added to `Branch` later joins the model and not this response. This is deliberately **not** `GET /admin/branches` with the permission relaxed: an endpoint's audience is part of its contract, and one endpoint serving two audiences has to get the difference right on every future change. **Soft-deleted branches never appear** — a closed premises must not keep advertising an address and a phone number. `opening_hours_ar` is free multiline Arabic text, displayed verbatim and **never parsed** (§7); `google_maps_url` is an absolute `https://` URL or `null`, and a client must degrade gracefully when it is null rather than fabricate a link. Ordered `display_order ASC NULLS LAST`, then `name` (correct Arabic order via the native collation), then `id`. **Paginated (TD-10):** `?page=` (default 1) and `?page_size=` (default 25, max 100 — capped, not refused).

get.description: TD-3.4, §5.2 (Revision 43). **Public at the caller's tier**, mounted beside the grid it is opened from: an anonymous visitor sees a public session's existence and details, and **never its private recordings**. Returns `{ occurrence, notes, recordings, linked_content, suggested_recording_name }`. **`occurrence` is byte-identical to the grid's** — TD-3.4 says *the occurrence above, plus …*, and one `include` and one mapper serve both, because two that agree today are two that drift. **`recordings` and `linked_content` are disjoint, and the split is the item's `origin` (R99.10):** «التسجيلات» are the linked contents with `origin = session_recording`; the rest are materials, and the **MIME type decides only which player and which download the reader gets**. The superseded rule — *linked content whose MIME begins `audio/` is a recording* — was wrong in both directions: it called every attached audio file a recording whether or not it was one, and it made a video recording of a صوت وصورة class unrepresentable. **`suggested_recording_name` is R75.6's default name for the NEXT recording of this occurrence**, composed by the server from the class and the date and numbered ` 2`, ` 3` against what is already linked, whatever produced it — a browser recording and the platform's own capture of the same lesson share one namespace, so they cannot land on the same name. It is numbered against **the titles this caller can see**: a suffix derived from an item the caller may not see would report that the item exists (§20 rule 17), and the ingestion worker's own allocation under a row lock is what makes the unattended path collision-free. It is a suggestion and never an invariant — nothing reads it back. Both lists pass **the same §4.9 tier rule the library list applies** — literally the same predicate, exported rather than restated — so a change to the tiers cannot reach one surface without the other, and BR-2's `consent_forced_private` exclusion holds here too. Each item is exactly `id`, `title`, `subject_id`, `level_id`: enough to open it **inside the Educational Library** (§5.2 — one reader, one permission path), and deliberately not the object location, which only `GET /content/{id}/download-url` (TD-3.5) hands out after its own check. **`notes` is always `null` and the key is present on purpose:** TD-3.4 names it and §5.2 lists notes on the page, but **§7 gives `Session` no notes column and defines no note entity** — `User.notes` is a different field on a different model. Adding one is a §7 schema decision and therefore the Document Owner's, exactly like the deferred `EducationalContent` uploader field. Shipping the key null keeps a client coded against TD-3.4 finding the field where the specification says it is, and keeps the gap **visible rather than silent**. **R109 — gated by the same tier as the grid.** A caller who may not read the occurrence receives `404`, never `403`: a distinguishable refusal would confirm that the hidden class exists (§20 rule 17), which is exactly what the tier prevents.

get.description: TD-3.10 (Revision 36) — everything the calendar screen needs to render its **chrome**, in one anonymous read: the Hijri mapping for every day in the range, the month metadata behind the dual title, and the Category, Level and Branch lists for the filters. `GET /calendar` keeps returning **only** occurrences, so the page makes exactly **two** requests and never a third. **Reference data only** — events, enrolments, progress and grades are never admissible here whatever a future screen would find convenient; that limit is what keeps a bootstrap from becoming a dumping ground. **Not a list endpoint, so TD-10 does not apply**: the contained lists are bounded by the domain (3 categories, ~21 levels, ≤10 branches, ≤366 days), and paginating a filter would be meaningless because a caller cannot use half of one. `hijri.months` and `gregorian_months` are what let the client render *يوليوز 2026 | محرم 1448* — or the two-month form across a boundary — with **no month-transition logic of its own**. A day whose Hijri month is not recorded and published omits its `hijri_*` fields (Revision 31: the platform says nothing rather than computing). **Cacheable**: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` plus a strong `ETag`, chosen against what actually changes — recording a Hijri month is not something a visitor must see within seconds, while an event edit is, which is why `/calendar` stays uncached. **`?category_id=` narrows the Level list, server-side**: §4.4 requires the restriction to happen here *"so the client never filters a list it was handed"*, so selecting a Category on the screen is a request rather than a local filter. It scopes **only** the Level list — the Hijri days, month metadata, Categories and Branches are the calendar's chrome regardless of which Category is selected. An unknown id yields an **empty** Level list rather than falling back to all Levels, because a filter that quietly stops filtering is worse than one returning nothing; a malformed id is `400`.

get.description: The one **public** read in the system (TD-3.4): an anonymous visitor receives the **public tier only**. One unified grid over the recurring **Group** timetable and the one-off **Event** exception layer, expanded across `from`..`to` (max 366 days — an unbounded range would expand every recurrence forever). All five recurrence types are supported; **biweekly-alternating** is week-on/week-off. **This endpoint never returns `401`** (Revision 34): a missing credential is anonymous, and an invalid, malformed or expired one is **ignored** and the request proceeds as anonymous — a credential that fails verification carries no identity to act on, and the landing page (§5.1) renders this calendar for visitors who have none. **Visibility is resolved server-side from the caller's live roles, never from a parameter** (§4.4): a Pending account sees exactly what an anonymous visitor sees; an approved Student or Parent adds the private tier, which is deliberately **not** filtered by the student's own branch (Risk R-6); a Teacher additionally sees Hidden events whose scope intersects their assigned groups; **all Admins see Hidden regardless of branch scope** while their Private tier **is** branch-scoped; Super Admins see everything. A group timetable is not public information, so an anonymous caller receives no groups. When scoped to a branch, nothing before its `operational_start_date` is returned (§4.4). **Instructors carry a resolved name (Revision 36.1)**: `instructors: [{ id, display_name }]`, where `display_name` is **already** `public_display_name` when the person set one and their full name otherwise. **Clients render it verbatim and implement no fallback** — a client-side `publicName || fullName` would be a second source of truth for which name a person agreed to publish, and the wrong branch leaks a legal name. **Each occurrence is self-sufficient (Revision 36)**: `description`, `recurrence`, `branch_name`, `room_name`, `category_id`/`category_name`, `level_id`/`level_name` and `instructors` travel with it, so an event dialog opens with **no further request** — the alternative was an N+1 on a public screen. Fields a kind has no source for are `null` rather than invented: an Event has no room or instructor, a Group no description or recurrence, because a Group *is* the routine timetable. A `category_id` filter joins `branch_id`/`level_id`/`group_id`; a Group inherits its category through its Level. Every occurrence also carries the **decorative Hijri overlay** (`hijri_date`, `hijri_month_ar`), read from the Ministry of Habous's official announcements as recorded in `HijriMonthStart` and resolved server-side (Revisions 31–32). **Nothing is computed and there is no day-offset** — the former adjustable ±2-day offset was removed, because an offset approximates a sighting-based calendar *uniformly* while the real divergence varies month to month. A month that has not been recorded **and published** carries `null` in both fields, and the client then renders the Gregorian date alone rather than a guess (§20 rule 14). It is a label: nothing in scheduling or recurrence reads it back (§4.4, §5.7). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` and times `HH:MM`, local wall-clock (TD-11) — a 09:00 class stays at 09:00 across Morocco's Ramadan DST shift (§19.2). **TD-3.4 filter set (R43), identical for anonymous and authenticated callers:** `from`, `to`, `academic_year_id`, `category_id`, `level_id`, `subject_id`, `branch_id`, `administrative_group_id`, `teacher_id`. **A filter a kind cannot satisfy excludes that kind rather than being ignored** — an Event has no subject, no academic year and no instructors, so `subject_id`, `academic_year_id` or `teacher_id` narrows the grid to Sessions; silently ignoring them would return Events that do not match what was asked. `teacher_id` matches the SESSION's own staffing snapshot, not the schedule's (R43.4): a teacher who covered one occurrence finds it, and one removed from the schedule does not lose the ones they actually took. **Sessions carry `subject_id`, `subject_name`, `teaching_mode`, `audience_label` and `status`** (R43); `audience_label` is who the class is *for* — the Administrative Group's name, the Teaching Group's, or the Level's, by mode — and it previously travelled inside `description`, which meant a Session's description held something that was not one. A **cancelled** session still appears: the calendar's job is to say a class is not happening, not to hide that it was scheduled. **`prefilled_filters` is returned for an authenticated caller** and is `null` for an anonymous one — *there is nothing to prefill* and *nothing was unambiguous* are different answers. It changes where the dropdowns **start**, never what they offer and never what the results are; the §4.4 tiers still filter every set. **A value is prefilled only when unambiguous:** a student enrolled in three Levels has no single own Level, and picking one would open their calendar on a third of their own timetable while looking like it showed all of it — so plural yields `null`, never *first*. **R109 — every kind now carries a tier, and this read applies it to all three.** §4.4's *Sessions are PUBLIC* and §4.6's *an exam has no visibility tier of its own* are superseded; every row that existed before the revision was backfilled `public`, so the browsable timetable is unchanged in fact. **`hidden` is narrowed to ownership**: the responsible person for that item — `EventStaff.responsible`, the occurrence's own `SessionStaff.teacher` (resolved on **its own date**, R91), or `ExamStaff.supervisor` — plus Super Admins. §4.4's *and to ALL Admins regardless of branch scope* is **withdrawn**, which is the one place this revision removes reach somebody had.

get.description: SRS Revisions 31–32, §5.7. The platform **reproduces exactly the official Hijri calendar published by the Ministry of Habous and Islamic Affairs** — never Umm al-Qura, never a library algorithm, and there is no day-offset (the Ministry's divergence varies month to month, so a uniform offset cannot express it). Always returns **twelve** rows: a month the Ministry has not yet announced is a blank to fill, not a missing row. **Super Admin only** (Revision 26 reference data), enforced server-side — the `/admin/*` prefix is not the permission boundary. **The response also carries `coverage`** — `published_through`, `days_remaining`, `warning` and `next_unrecorded` — which is the safeguard against the one failure mode a manually-maintained calendar has. Automation is impossible **by the nature of the source, not by preference**: Morocco declares months on *actual moon sighting*, announced the evening before, so every computable calendar (Umm al-Qura, tabular, astronomical conjunction) diverges from the official one unpredictably, and an automated overlay would be *confidently wrong* rather than silent. Silence is the correct behaviour when a month is unannounced — `baseHijri` returns `null` and dates render Gregorian-only — but a calendar that runs out **in silence** is how this feature stops working unnoticed. So the coverage is reported on the screen that exists to maintain it. It **computes no Hijri date**: it is arithmetic on Gregorian dates the Ministry itself supplied. `days_remaining` counts to the **29-day floor**, not 30, because day 30 resolves only when the next consecutive month is recorded; it **goes negative** rather than clamping, since *expired 40 days ago* and *expires today* call for different urgency; and it is `null` — never `0` — when nothing is published, because *nobody has recorded anything* and *it ran out today* are different answers. **Only published months count** (§5.7 renders only those; a draft is runway the platform will not use).

Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, local calendar dates (TD-11), never instants.

Soft delete with a `Trash` snapshot, like every other deletion (TD-5, BR-15). **Super Admin only**, asserted in the service. **TD-15: `version` is REQUIRED**, as a query parameter rather than a body — withdrawing a month somebody else has just corrected is the identical hazard a correction guards against, and a `DELETE` with a body is refused by proxies. **Only the LAST recorded month may be withdrawn** (`LATER_MONTH_RECORDED`, naming the month that blocks it): the months are a contiguous sequence and §5.7's conversion walks it, so a hole would surface to a reader as *missing Ministry data* rather than as the deletion that caused it. **Publication is not a second obstacle** — §5.7 already treats a correction as returning a month to `draft`, so a withdrawal is the stronger form of something the specification permits; what is refused is the hole, visible or not.

Re-running is therefore idempotent. Imported months land as **`draft`**, because Umm al-Qura is calculated and the two calendars differ by a day with some regularity, so nothing derived is displayed until the year is reviewed and published. Provenance is recorded per value in `source` (`umm_al_qura_icu`). **No network call at any time** — the tables come from the Node build's own ICU — and **no read path consults the baseline**: after the insert the row is an ordinary row, corrected through `PUT /admin/hijri-calendar/{year}/{month}` under TD-15. A month whose derived date would violate the ordering invariant against already-stored neighbours is skipped rather than failing the year. Super Admin only; audited once for the act (TD-8).

get.summary: Pick a person while doing operational work
get.description: **Owner clarification, 2026-08-28 — the operational half of what `/admin/users` used to be.** Admin **or** Super Admin. It answers *who may I staff, enrol or roster*, and it is a **deliberately smaller projection**: exactly `id`, `name_arabic`, `nickname` and `roles`. No email, no phone, no `account_status`, no TD-15 `version` — a picker can do nothing that would need them, and five operational screens were receiving every user's contact details in order to render a list of names. **The scope rule is NOT relaxed**: it is the same branch-scoped query `/admin/users` runs (§4.2 R25), shared rather than reimplemented so the two cannot drift on which rows a branch-scoped Admin may see while differing on what is returned about them. Same filters (`role`, `branch_id`, `beneficiaries_only`), same TD-10 search and paging. **Why two endpoints rather than one with a relaxed role:** the representations are not identical — the Document Owner's standing preference for one endpoint with role-scoped data applies where two would return *the same* representation, and these deliberately do not.

get.description: **SUPER ADMIN ONLY (Owner clarification, 2026-08-28).** This is global ACCOUNT administration — every person on the platform, their address, their status, their roles, and the power to edit, suspend or delete the account itself — and it is separated from *managing operational data*, which an Admin does. An Admin receives `403` on this endpoint and on **every** write beneath it, asserted in the service so the refusal reaches every caller including tests and jobs; hiding the menu entry is not the enforcement. An Admin who needs to pick a person uses `/admin/directory`. **The refusal is uniform and therefore non-disclosing:** the same `403` comes back for an out-of-scope user, a user inside the caller's own branch, and an id that does not exist, so §20 rule 17's property is preserved by uniformity rather than by answering `404`. §14.2 Users screen. Columns are exactly what §14.2 specifies — Arabic name, Nickname, Role(s), Branch scope, Status, Phone — and deliberately nothing from `StudentSocialProfile`, which §4.10 restricts to assigned teachers. Visibility is branch-scoped (§4.2 Revision 25): a branch-scoped Admin sees only users holding a live role assignment to one of that Admin's managed branches, and users with **no** branch assignment — parents, unassigned students, pre-provisioned accounts — are visible to **Super Admins only**. An all-branches (`NULL`) Admin sees everyone. The `branch_id` filter narrows within that scope and can never reach outside it. Filters: `role`, `branch_id`, `status` (§14.2). TD-10 search via `q` spans Arabic name, French name, nickname, phone, the linked parent's name, and Google email across **both** `UserIdentity.email` and `User.pre_provisioned_email` (Revision 15) — an unclaimed account has no identity row, and those are the accounts staff most need to find. Substring, case-insensitive, minimum 2 characters, matched against indexed normalized shadow columns; the query is normalized by the same rules as the stored value, with parity against the SQL functions asserted by test. Sorted by `name_arabic` (natively ar-x-icu collated, TD-6a) with `id` as the deterministic tiebreaker. Paginated: default 25, max 100. **`?beneficiaries_only=true` (R79.7)** returns exactly the institute's مستفيدات — the durable `is_beneficiary` fact, **independent of every role and of every enrolment**. A minor beneficiary holds no role row at all (§4.3) and is included; a مؤطرة who also studies is included while one who does not is not; a beneficiary between placements, or never yet placed, is included, because enrolment is BACKFILL EVIDENCE and never the runtime definition — it would otherwise be the precondition for being enrollable. **The flag itself is never published** (R79.8): the screens that need it read it server-side, exactly as `sex` is handled.

The binding happens on that address's first successful Google login (TD-4.10). The email is stored lowercase (TD-12) and is unique among non-null values via a TD-6 partial index spanning deleted users too, so an address can never be made claimable twice. Admin or Super Admin (TD-2) with the TD-12 freshness assertion; only a Super Admin may create another Admin. delete.description: **R111/R112 — Super Admin only** (Document Owner, 2026-08-28); an Admin receives `403`, asserted in the service. Behaves exactly as `DELETE /profile` does, **on the same three-day window**: one rule and one mechanism, so a deletion clicked by mistake stays recoverable, which an immediate purge would not be. **`?permanent=true`** performs R111's de-identification **now** instead of after the window. It is **the same operation the window reaches, not a stronger one** — no row is removed, and every preserved relationship survives exactly as it would have. The tombstone keeps its structural columns (`id`, `sex` — §4.4b evaluates Level restrictions against it, so a preserved enrolment must still make sense — `account_status`, `created_at`, `is_beneficiary`) and loses its complete identifying surface: composed and split names, contact/public identity, request metadata, notes and external identifiers. Credentials, role assignments, planning data and both email-ownership channels are removed; the ownerless normalized-email lock row remains to serialize the next claimant. The recoverable Trash snapshot is removed in the same transaction so it cannot retain the erased PII. The **TD-10 search shadows are trigger-maintained and follow**, so the original remains unsearchable. **Idempotent**: running it twice changes nothing, because a de-identification that half-ran is worse than one that has not run. The same two refusals apply — *sooner* must not mean *with fewer checks*.

patch.description: §5.6 `/admin/users` *"edit"*, §14.2, TD-15 optimistic locking. Body: `{ version, name_arabic?, name_french?, nickname?, phone? }` — **strictly** those keys. **`account_status` is refused, not ignored**: suspension carries TD-4.15's obligation to revoke every live `RefreshToken` **in the same transaction**, so a client that set the field here and received `200` would believe access had been withdrawn while a 30-day credential was still live. It is the same reasoning that makes `PATCH /sessions/{id}` refuse `status`. **`pre_provisioned_email` is refused** because it authorises *claiming* an account (§7 R15) — editing it after the fact would hand a half-registered person's account to someone else — and **`public_display_name`** because §20 rule 21 resolves the published identity server-side, and a back-office form is exactly where a second answer to *which name did this person publish* would appear. **A user outside a branch Admin's §4.2 R25 visibility answers `404`, never `403`** (§20 rule 17): saying *exists, but not yours* is itself the disclosure that rule prevents. TD-12 freshness applies — user-management mutations re-read the caller's live status and role on every request. The **TD-10 search shadow columns are maintained by a database trigger**, never by this handler; a second normalization would drift from the one the indexes were built with and make search find some rows and not others. The audit row records **which fields changed, not their values** — a name and a phone number are personal data, and TD-8's record must not become a second copy of them.

post.description: §5.6 *"deactivate"*, **TD-1 `Active → Suspended`**, **TD-4.15**. Body: `{ version, reason }`. **Every live session is revoked in the same transaction** — TD-12 requires suspension to take effect on the next refresh *immediately*, and a suspension that commits without revoking leaves a 30-day credential alive, which is precisely the safeguarding failure the freshness rule exists to prevent. The `auth.token_revoked` audit row names the affected session ids, so a specific session stays attributable. **The reason is mandatory and may not be blank**, for the reason a cancellation's is: it is the only record of why access was withdrawn, and afterwards nobody can reconstruct it. **Refused from any status but `Active`** (`409 STATE_CONFLICT`, `reason: INVALID_TRANSITION`) — TD-1 allows the transition from nowhere else. **You cannot suspend your own account** (`reason: SELF_SUSPENSION`): the administrator is locked out by their own next request, and the recovery path is a VPS shell. **Nor the last active Super Admin** (`reason: LAST_SUPER_ADMIN`) — Revision 22 documents that lockout as a *recovery* path requiring `DATABASE_URL` and a manual seed run, not an outcome a back-office control may produce with one click.

put.summary: Replace a user's role and branch-scope assignments
put.description: §5.6 *"role/branch-scope assignment"*, §14.2, TD-2. Body: `{ assignments: [{ role, branch_id }] }` — **the complete set the user should hold afterwards**. A `PUT` of the whole set rather than add/remove verbs: the set is what an administrator reasons about, one call yields one audit row describing one decision, and **there is no window in which the user holds half of an intended change** — which add-then-remove creates every time a role moves between branches. **`branch_id: null` means all branches for that assignment** (§7 R24), never *no branch*; it is a required, explicitly nullable key rather than an optional one, so the unscoped grant is never the easiest thing to type by accident. **Removal is a soft delete** (TD-5) — a revoked assignment is tombstoned, so *"who was an administrator at this branch in March"* stays answerable, and re-granting an identical assignment revives that row rather than colliding with the unique index that spans deleted rows. **Only a Super Admin may grant or revoke `admin` or `super_admin`**; an Admin doing either is privilege propagation, the same rule `POST /admin/users` applies to creation. **`super_admin` IS assignable here**, unlike at creation: Revision 22 states that after bootstrap *every subsequent change of administrators happens exclusively through the application*, and refusing the role would leave a VPS shell as the only route to a second Super Admin. **The last active Super Admin cannot lose the role** (`409 STATE_CONFLICT`, `reason: LAST_SUPER_ADMIN`). **Sessions are deliberately NOT revoked** — Revision 10 resolves this trade-off explicitly: every safeguarding-sensitive operation re-asserts live assignments per request, so a revoked role stops mattering immediately where it matters, and the enumerated RefreshRevokedReason values in §7 cover logout, safeguarding actions, replay and the R101 one-time rollout; none honestly describes a demotion.

The transaction locks the singleton first and both User rows in deterministic id order, updates the one relationship atomically, increments its version and audits UUID coordinates. It does not remove the former owner's Super Admin assignment or grant one to the target. Suspension, deletion, de-identification and demotion of the current owner are refused until a successful transfer.

get.description: **Read access is retained for Admins** (branch-scoped) because operational work depends on it — a Group references a Branch, a Level and a Room (TD-2 Revision 26). Ordered by display_order ASC NULLS LAST then name (ar-x-icu collated, §2.2/TD-10). Super Admins see all. **Paginated (TD-10):** `?page=` (default 1) and `?page_size=` (default 25, **max 100** — a larger request is capped, not refused). Responds `{ data, meta: { page, page_size, total } }`; `total` is the unpaginated count, so a client can compute page count. Ordering carries an `id` tiebreaker, which is what keeps paging stable across requests. **Explicit contract DTO (§16.2, Revision 38):** every branch response — here, `POST` and `PATCH` alike — returns exactly `id`, `name`, `operational_start_date`, `display_order`, `address`, `phone`, `email`, `opening_hours_ar`, `google_maps_url` and `version`, in `snake_case`, built by an allow-list projection. `operational_start_date` is a **TD-11 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`)**, never an instant — an instant invites a timezone conversion in a client. `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at` and `deleted_by` are **not** exposed: they are operational metadata no screen consumes. Until Revision 38 this endpoint returned the Prisma row itself, which is how a `camelCase` shape and four internal columns came to sit inside a `snake_case` envelope; a column added to `Branch` now joins the model and not this response. **Sorting (R76.1-R76.3):** optional `?sort_by=&sort_dir=asc|desc`. `sort_by` names a field in the CONTRACT and is matched against this endpoint's own allow-list — anything outside it is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, never ignored and never passed through to a query, so there is no path from a query string to a column. Absent, BR-19's order is preserved exactly. Every resolved order ends in an `id` tiebreaker, without which offset pagination can put a row on two pages or on neither. Allowed here: `name`, `operational_start_date`.

get.description: TD-3.12 (Revision 43) — the permanent **organisational** unit inside a Level (§4.4c). **Operational data**: Admin within branch scope, or Super Admin, asserted in the service (TD-2) — the `/admin/` prefix authenticates but does not authorise. A branch-scoped Admin sees only the groups of the branches they administer; an all-branches (`NULL`) scope means *every* branch, never *none*. `?level_id=` and `?branch_id=` narrow within that scope and can never reach outside it; a **malformed** id is `400`, not an empty list, because "that is not an id" and "this Level has no groups" are different answers and the second one misleads. Ordered by `display_order` then `name` — natively `ar-x-icu` collated (TD-6a), so correct Arabic ordering needs no per-query COLLATE (§20 rule 13). **Paginated (TD-10):** `?page=` (default 1), `?page_size=` (default 25, max 100 — capped, not refused). **Explicit contract DTO (§16.2):** exactly `id`, `name`, `level_id`, `branch_id`, `display_order`, `member_count` and `version`. `member_count` is how many live enrolments the group holds, **derived per request and never stored** — a stored count drifts the moment an enrolment is made from any other screen, and the §8 management table depends on it being true. **`branch_id` is load-bearing** (§4.4c): it is the single answer to *"which branch is this person at"*, which `User.intended_branch_id` deliberately does not give — that records only what an applicant asked for (§4.1, R39). Absent by design and never to be re-added (§20 rule 22): `room_id`, `teacher_id`, `assistant_id`, the weekly schedule, and **`max_students`** — there is no capacity anywhere in the model, informational or otherwise (BR-23), and `CAPACITY_FULL` is retired from the TD-3.8 catalogue. **Sorting (R76.1-R76.3):** optional `?sort_by=&sort_dir=asc|desc`. `sort_by` names a field in the CONTRACT and is matched against this endpoint's own allow-list — anything outside it is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, never ignored and never passed through to a query, so there is no path from a query string to a column. Absent, BR-19's order is preserved exactly. Every resolved order ends in an `id` tiebreaker, without which offset pagination can put a row on two pages or on neither. Allowed here: `name`.

The Level and the Branch are both re-checked **live and non-soft-deleted inside the transaction** — a foreign key alone would accept a closed premises. This is the route for **additional** groups: a Level always already has one, created atomically with it (TD-4.6b, Revision 43.1), or backfilled at the first Branch (TD-4.6d), so a Level is never grouplessness-by-omission.

post.description: TD-3.12, §5.6. Body: `{ student_id }` — **strictly** that one key. **`level_id` is not accepted**: the service reads it from the group, because taking it from the caller would leave the composite FK as the only thing between a typo and a mis-filed student, surfacing as an opaque constraint error rather than a decision this service made. The response echoes `level_id` so the client learns which Level the student was thereby enrolled into. **`Level.gender_restriction` is enforced** (Revision 27) and a `null` `sex` is *not eligible* rather than a wildcard. **BR-21 — one group per Level — is refused with an explanation, not a raw constraint error:** enrolling into the same group again is `409 DUPLICATE`, and enrolling into a *different* group of a Level the student already belongs to is `409 STATE_CONFLICT` with `reason: ALREADY_ENROLLED_IN_LEVEL` naming `current_administrative_group_id`, which is exactly the information needed to decide whether to move them instead. **There is NO capacity check** (BR-23): none exists, `CAPACITY_FULL` is retired from the TD-3.8 catalogue, and the roster row lock went with the invariant it protected — a future capacity rule must bring the lock back rather than rely on a constraint alone. **Enqueues `consent.reevaluate` for each SESSION whose resolved audience now contains the student, in the same transaction** (§4.1a, TD-7, Revision 43): BR-2's subject is a session's audience, so the gate can never drift from the records.

get.description: TD-3.12 (Revision 43), §4.4c, **BR-22**. Returns `{ groups, split, unassigned }` — **the whole split in one read**, because the unassigned list is unreadable without the groups beside it: the screen's question is *who is not placed, and where could they go*, and two round trips would let a client render half the answer. **`split` is not redundant with `groups.length`:** a Subject with no Teaching Groups is taught to the entire Level (§4.4c), so an empty `unassigned` there means *the question does not apply*, whereas an empty `unassigned` on a **split** Subject means *everyone is placed*. The two render identically without the flag and one of them is an alarm. **`unassigned` is BR-22 made visible** — students enrolled in the Level holding no seat for this split Subject have **no sessions for it at all**, and nothing else in the platform would say so. **Not paginated:** a page boundary drawn through that list would let a beneficiary receiving no teaching fall onto page two. **Branch-scoped for an Admin, unscoped for a Super Admin** (Revision 43.3), so a branch Admin correctly sees a *partial* unassigned list — their own students, the only ones they may place. Each group carries `member_count`, so answering *how many are in this split* costs no request per group. **No `branch_id` on a group** (§4.4c): it belongs to a Subject and a Level, and a Level spans branches (§4.4b).

Without that split a Marrakesh Admin could delete the Quran split that Targa's students depend on while seeing only Marrakesh students in the unassigned list: authority over everyone, visibility of some. Creating these is **not** a prerequisite for teaching: a Subject with no rows here is taught to the entire Level.

get.description: §5.6 *"Levels"*, §14.1 مستويات, §4.4b. Admin+ read (TD-2 R26); Teachers excluded (R30). **Ordered by Category first**, because §7 scopes a Level's `display_order` *within* its Category and a flat ordering would interleave two curricula. `?category_id=` narrows **server-side**, so the client never filters a list the server owns; a malformed value is `400`, not a silently unfiltered list. Each row carries **`default_visibility`** — §4.9's default content tier for that Level, resolved through its Category (`content.default_visibility.category.{id}`, §15.1). It rides the Level because §14.1's upload screen must *honour* the default and that screen loads Levels, not Categories; a default the screen cannot read is one it cannot honour. **Unpaginated** — a Levels screen that hides its second page cannot answer *"does this Level already exist"*. Each row carries `group_count`, `subject_count` and `enrollment_count`: without them the delete control is a guess and the only way to find out is to press it. Each row also carries **`description`** (NEW L, 2026-08-27) — a short sentence saying what the Level is, **nullable and ordinarily so**. It is editable on the Level, and the launch baseline reads `المستوى N - برنامج X`; that text is **seeded data, not a format the API imposes**, so a Super Admin may write anything. `category_name` travels as a **label** for grouping, never as an identifier — `category_id` is that. **No `branch_id`**: a Level is Category-scoped and branch-independent and may hold groups at several branches (§4.4b). **Sorting (R76.1-R76.3):** optional `?sort_by=&sort_dir=asc|desc`. `sort_by` names a field in the CONTRACT and is matched against this endpoint's own allow-list — anything outside it is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, never ignored and never passed through to a query, so there is no path from a query string to a column. Absent, BR-19's order is preserved exactly. Every resolved order ends in an `id` tiebreaker, without which offset pagination can put a row on two pages or on neither. Allowed here: `name`, `category`. **`?eligible_for_student=` (R27 + BR-21, 2026-08-18)** narrows to the Levels THAT BENEFICIARY may enter. The dependency runs beneficiary → Levels because that is the business question — *where may she be enrolled* — rather than *whom does this Level permit*; the reverse was tried and reversed, because a woman already enrolled in one Level is still a beneficiary. Two rules narrow: a Level whose restriction she cannot satisfy is withheld (a NULL `sex` cannot PROVE eligibility, and the placement would be refused anyway), and the one Level she already holds a live enrolment in is excluded — **only that exact pair**, since one beneficiary may hold many enrolments, one per Level. An unknown beneficiary narrows to nothing rather than back to everything. **`sex` is not published and is not added by this filter**: the eligible SET travels and the fact behind it never leaves the service (§4.10, BR-16).

get.description: TD-3.12, §4.4 — the **unit of delivery**. **Role-scoped on one endpoint** (Document Owner decision, 2026-08-05): Super Admin sees everything, a branch Admin sees their branches, and a **Teacher sees exactly the schedules they staff** (§4.4c — `CourseScheduleStaff` is the single teacher-scope resolution). Everyone else is refused. `/admin/` is a **routing namespace, not an authorization boundary** — the representation a teacher needs is byte-identical to an administrator's, so a second route returning the same shape would be duplication, not separation. **Reading is not managing:** creating, editing, deleting and `/conflicts` remain Admin, because §14.1 says teachers *do not create or edit schedules*. A teacher who staffs nothing receives an **empty list, not a `403`** — they may ask the question, and their scope resolves to nothing. An explicit `branch_id` can **narrow** a caller's reach but never widen it, since both conditions must hold. Asserted in the service (TD-2). `?branch_id=`, `?subject_id=` and `?academic_year_id=` narrow **within** that scope and can never reach outside it; an all-branches (`NULL`) scope means *every* branch, never *none* (§7, R24). **Paginated (TD-10)**, ordered by start then end time — a timetable reads by clock, and `start_time` is a **wall-clock** `TIME(0)` column (TD-11), not an instant. **The DTO carries `teaching_mode` + `target_id`, never the three nullable target columns** (§4.4c): a response holding two of them would have no correct reading, and one field cannot express that state at all. Times render as `HH:MM` and `anchor_date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` — an ISO instant for either would invite a client to shift a class that starts at 15:00 at its branch, which is the exact bug TD-11 separates the two kinds of value to prevent. **`level_id` names WHICH LEVEL the class is for (2026-08-18)**, resolved server-side whatever the mode names: for `entire_level` it equals `target_id`, and for the other two it comes through the target, whose own row is the only thing that knows it (§2.2) — a Group-taught class has `level_id IS NULL` on its own row, because the CHECK behind §4.4c allows exactly one target per mode. It is a RESOLVED field and not a second target: it cannot contradict `target_id`, and the two group columns remain absent. `null` on a write response, like the labels beside it, since a caller that just submitted knows the Level. **R97 — `delivery_mode` and `online_media_mode`.** `in_person` (the default, and what every class scheduled before this revision was) or `online`; an online class **requires** `online_media_mode` (`audio_video` | `audio_only`) and **must carry no `room_id`** — both directions are refused rather than dropped, and both are database CHECKs as well. Sending a room alongside `online` is refused; the schedule's `branch_id` is untouched, because a Branch is the class's administrative and educational scope and not its venue (R92), so a class delivered عن بُعد is still that branch's class. patch.description: TD-3.12, §4.4, TD-1, TD-15. **A field edit, not a transition.** Body: `{ version, date?, start_time?, end_time?, room_id?, delivery_mode?, online_media_mode?, visibility?, staff? }` — **strictly** those keys. **`status` is refused**: cancelling and restoring are TD-1 transitions carrying obligations a field assignment cannot — a cancellation must state a reason and record how many people it affected, a restore is refused once the date has passed — so accepting `status` here would give the state machine a second entrance with none of that attached. **`schedule_id` is refused** too: moving an occurrence to another schedule detaches it from the recurrence that explains it, leaving a row no schedule edit will ever reach again. **The write always marks the row `overridden`, even when the new values equal the schedule's** (Revision 43.4): the flag records that *a human decided about this occurrence*, which is what must survive the next schedule edit — inferring it from *differs from the schedule* would silently un-protect a session whose schedule later moved to match it. **`staff` supplied REPLACES this occurrence's snapshot; omitted leaves it untouched** — an empty array is therefore a real instruction (*this session has no staff*) and deliberately not the same as omission. A **held** session cannot be rescheduled (`409 ALREADY_HELD`). **Not under `/admin/`**, deliberately: TD-2 gives a Teacher write access to the sessions they staff, so the prefix would misdescribe the audience; scope is asserted in the service, which is the only place that knows who staffs what, and anything out of reach answers `404` (§20 rule 17). **R97 — `delivery_mode` and `online_media_mode`, this occurrence's own.** On exactly the footing `room_id` has: they change THIS date and nothing else, and the `overridden` flag this endpoint always sets is what protects the change from the next schedule resync. **There is no parallel "online override" endpoint** — this one represents it, and a second would be two ways to say *this occurrence differs*. The same equivalence the schedule boundary enforces applies here from one shared check, so an occurrence can never reach a combination a schedule could not: online **requires** a media mode and **clears** the room; in-person refuses a media mode. **No provider data (R97.9).** **R109 — `visibility`, this occurrence's own.** On exactly the footing `room_id` has: it changes THIS date and nothing else, and the `overridden` flag this endpoint always sets is what protects it from the next schedule resync. Optional `delivery_mode=in_person|online` makes the appraisal modality-aware. post.description: **§4.4c, §4.3, R97, R98.** Mints a **short-lived participant credential** for one online occurrence. The durable rule this endpoint exists to hold: **بذور الأمل authorizes; the media provider executes the media session** — never the reverse. Authorization completes before a credential exists, and it is the platform's own: the R92 audience for a beneficiary (through the single `audienceForSession`, never a second query), R91 effective staffing for a مؤطِّرة (`SessionStaff` first, then the schedule's assignments **effective on this occurrence's date**), the branch scope that already edits the occurrence for an administrator, and §4.3's approved `FamilyLink` for a guardian. **The body is empty and `.strict()`** — participant identity, room, role, grants and expiry are all derived server-side, so a client cannot name its own identity, ask for teaching permissions, or choose a room. An **assistant receives identical operational authority to the main مؤطِّرة** (R87 §G); **R88 declared capability grants nothing**. A **guardian acting for a linked child enters AS THE CHILD** — the credential carries the child's identity and display name, never the guardian's, and she gains no beneficiary role by it. **Only an `online` occurrence can be joined** (`409 NOT_ONLINE` for an in-person one), and only inside the **join window**: fifteen minutes before the scheduled start until thirty minutes after the scheduled end, on server time (`409 BEFORE_WINDOW` / `AFTER_WINDOW`, each carrying `opens_at` and `closes_at`). **The window is evaluated AFTER authorization**, so an unauthorised caller learns nothing about the timetable — anything out of reach is `404`, never `403` (§20 rule 17). **Nothing is persisted.** The room is **derived** from the Session's own identity (R97.9 — no vendor identifier on any schedule, session or occurrence projection, and no room table), so repeating the request creates no duplicate state and a page refresh costs nothing. **No API key or secret is ever returned**, no room-management capability is granted, and joining is **not attendance** (§4.7). Recording is a later revision and no recording grant is issued.

A مؤطِّرة who does not staff the occurrence is `404` as always. **Idempotent**: pressing it twice returns the recording already running rather than starting a second, and a partial unique index makes that true even for two simultaneous requests. **The provider is reached only after the platform has decided**, and the recording is captured **server-side** so a closed tab or a dropped connection does not lose the lesson. **No provider identifier appears on the response** (R97.9): the egress job id and the staging location are integration state.

Starting and stopping need teaching authority; **seeing** does not. **`null` is the ordinary answer and a real one** — recording is optional, so a class nobody recorded has no state, and the interface shows nothing rather than «لم يبدأ التسجيل» on every screen. **Carries no provider identifier** and no staging location. **`availability` is the ASSOCIATION's answer and `status` is the PROVIDER's, and they genuinely differ** (R99.14): `status = completed` means only that an object exists in a staging bucket, while `availability` walks `capturing → processing → importing → available`, with `import_failed` for an import that was refused and will be retried. **«available» is DERIVED from `educational_content_id` being set** — never a stored status value that could disagree with the object it describes — and that id is how a client opens the recording, through the ordinary content path. The provider is then asked to finish; **what actually happened is settled by its authenticated callback**, never by this response. The recording moves to `stopping` and then, on the provider's report, to `processing` and `completed`. **`completed` is NOT «available»** (R99.14): the asset exists at the provider, not yet in Bodour storage, and the interface must not claim otherwise. The verified completion callback then **enqueues `session-recording-ingest`** (C2), which verifies the actual bytes, copies them server-side into Bodour storage and creates the `EducationalContent` + `SessionContent`; only then does `availability` become `available`.
