post.summary: The recording provider reports on a job
post.description: **R99.15 — verified, never trusted.** The provider posts here when a recording starts, progresses, finishes or fails. **Authenticated by the provider's own signature over the RAW request body**, which only a holder of the API secret can produce — the route is mounted before the JSON parser precisely so those bytes survive, since a parsed-and-reserialised body no longer matches the signature. **It cannot manufacture anything.** Three things must all hold before a row changes: the signature verifies; the event names an egress job **this platform started**; and the transition is one the state machine allows. A job id nobody here has seen is ignored, so an arbitrary external request creates no recording and — even in later sections — no educational content. **Duplicate delivery is a no-op**: terminal states accept nothing, so a completion delivered three times yields one recording, and a late `recording` cannot un-finish a completed one. **A completion PERSISTS and ENQUEUES; it never imports** (C2). Copying a 500 MB MP4 inside this handler would hold the request open long enough for a provider to time out and **retry**, turning one slow import into several concurrent ones — so the handler writes the provider's fact and inserts a `session-recording-ingest` job **in the same transaction as the status write** (§16.2, §20 rule 8), singleton per recording, and returns. The job is enqueued **on the transition edge, not on the state**: a re-delivered completion finds the row already terminal and enqueues nothing. **Always answers `204`**, whatever it decided: a distinguishable refusal would tell a prober its guess was wrong, and a provider retrying forever against a `4xx` it cannot fix is worse than a silent discard. What actually happened is in the log. **Not in the guarded router** — the caller is a machine with no Bodour session — and it is the only route in this area outside it.

get.description: TD-3.13 (Revision 43), §5.2, §4.9. **PUBLIC and anonymous.** An invalid credential is *ignored* rather than refused, so this endpoint **never answers `401`** — a public surface that can `401` is not public. `?category_id=` `?level_id=` `?academic_year_id=` `?subject_id=` `?page=` `?page_size=`; **the filter set is identical for anonymous and authenticated callers**, and a signed-in-only filter would make navigation differ by audience, which §5.2 forbids. **Signing in REORDERS, it does not unlock:** the same set comes back in the §5.2 order — **own branch → Global → other branches**. `branch_id IS NULL` is *Global*, not *unknown* (§7), which is why it sorts second and not last: a platform-wide resource is more relevant to a reader than another branch's local one. A caller with no branch context has no first bucket and the ordering degrades without a special case; own branch resolves through `Enrollment → AdministrativeGroup.branch_id` for a member and through role scopes for staff (§7 names this ordering as one of the three things that resolve through that column). **§4.9's three tiers still apply, and that is not a contradiction of "nothing hidden":** TD-3.13's sentence is about *personalisation*, §5.2's *"identical filters never means identical results"* is about the tiers, which are a property of who the caller is rather than a personalisation. `public` is visible to everyone including anonymous; `private` to logged-in students enrolled in the target Level **and parents of such students** — resolved through approved `FamilyLink`s without requiring an `X-Active-Child-ID` context, since the library is one shared reading surface and a parent must be able to compare two children's materials; `hidden` is **excluded from Student/Parent directories** and visible to Admins and Teachers only. A **Pending** account sees the public tier exactly like an anonymous visitor (TD-1). **BR-2: `consent_forced_private` items are excluded from the public tier explicitly**, not merely trusted to have had their visibility moved by the re-evaluation engine — a hard constraint that holds only while a background job is current is a race, not a constraint. **Listing is not the download gate:** a restricted item appears with its `visibility` so a client can badge it, and `GET /content/{id}/download-url` (TD-3.5) performs the §4.9 check before any presigned URL is minted. **The DTO deliberately omits `storage_bucket`, `storage_key`, `original_filename` and `consent_forced_private`** — the first three are the object's location, and publishing them on a public endpoint would hand every anonymous visitor the input the permission check exists to protect; the fourth is a fact about a child. **Paginated (TD-10).** **Each item carries the §5.2 headings resolved server-side** — `category_id`/`category_name`, `level_name`, `subject_name`, `academic_year_label`, `branch_name` — because that view groups Category → Level → Academic Year → Branch and **no public endpoint publishes Subject or Academic Year names**: `/admin/subjects` and `/admin/academic-years` are Admin-only by design (R30), and `/calendar/bootstrap` carries Categories, Levels and Branches but neither of those. Carrying them makes the response self-sufficient, which TD-3.4 already requires of the calendar; the alternatives were widening that cached payload for an unrelated screen, or a new public reference surface exposing the whole curriculum to anonymous callers. **They are labels, never identifiers** — the ids remain what a client filters and links by. `branch_name` is `null` exactly where `branch_id` is, and that means **Global**, not unknown. **`suggested_recording_name` (R75.6, server-owned since R99)** sits beside `data`/`meta`: what to call a recording made from this screen, named after the Subject in view and the association's own date and numbered by the same shared rule. `null` when no Subject is in view — a name of nothing but a date identifies nothing. The rule lives on the server because R99 added a producer of recordings that is not a browser at all, and a rule one producer cannot reach is a rule implemented twice.

post.description: TD-3.5, §4.9, TD-9. **Phase one of two.** The browser then PUTs the file **straight to MinIO** through the returned `put_url`, so the file never passes through the API (§2.3 — a small VPS and mobile connections). Body: `{ filename, size, mime, content_meta }`; `content_meta` is `{ level_id, subject_id, academic_year_id, branch_id, visibility?, origin?, replaces_content_id? }`. **`origin` (R99.12) states what the thing IS** — `uploaded` (the default) or `session_recording` — because R99.10 makes «التسجيلات» a function of this field rather than of the MIME type, and §4.9's MVP flow is a مؤطِّرة recording on her phone and uploading the file: without it every such recording would arrive as a *material*. **It grants nothing.** `video/*` is still refused here whatever it says — TD-9's video row is reachable only by the platform's own ingestion pipeline (R99.8), and the whitelist check does not consult this field. Like the scope fields it is **bound into the ticket and never restated at `/complete`**, so the classification cannot be changed after the decision that authorised it. **`branch_id` is required and explicitly nullable** — `null` is the **Global / بدون فرع** scope (§4.9), an authorization-relevant value only an Admin may choose, so an absent key would make Global the silent default for a Teacher who forgot the field. **§4.9 Global-scope rule, enforced here:** only Super Admins and Admins may assign Global; a **Teacher is locked to the branches of the schedules they staff** (resolved through `CourseScheduleStaff` per §4.4c — the single definition of a teacher's reach, never the role assignment), and a Teacher passing `null` or an out-of-scope branch is refused. **Everything decidable before a byte moves is decided here** — the scope, the TD-9 MIME whitelist, the TD-9 size cap, and the per-user quota — because a teacher on a phone connection must learn they cannot publish Globally *before* uploading 80 MB. **`visibility` defaults to the Category setting** (`content.default_visibility.category.{id}`, §4.9/§15.1) when omitted. **The subject must actually be taught at the level** (`LevelSubject`, R43). **`replaces_content_id` (R53)** targets an existing record: the same flow runs and completion updates that row — a **new key with a new hash segment**, the old object quarantined, `version` incremented; keys are never reused or overwritten (TD-9, §20 rule 15). **The per-user quota is 30/hour**, counted in PostgreSQL **inside this transaction** under a row lock (TD-4.12, TD-15.2, Revision 14) — never in process memory, never through pg-boss. **`upload_id` is a signed ticket, not a database row:** §7 defines no pending-upload entity, and the ticket binds every authorization decision taken here so that `/complete` cannot restate them. `upload.gc` (TD-7) reaps objects older than 48 h that no content row claims.

post.description: TD-3.5, §4.9 (Revision 8), TD-9. **Phase two.** Verifies the object that was actually stored: a **ranged GET of `bytes=0-511`** for the magic bytes and a **HEAD** for the true size — the server **never streams or buffers the file** to validate it. A mismatch **deletes the object and creates no row**, answering **`409 VALIDATION_FAILED`**: the request was well-formed, the object was not what it claimed (TD-3.8 records this as the "409 variant on upload complete"). On success the `EducationalContent` row is created, or **updated when the ticket carries `replaces_content_id`** (R53). Body: `{ title, description? }` and **nothing else** — the scope, type, size and key were bound into the ticket at `/initiate` and are not re-openable from the body, for the same reason §4.1b refuses an email from the registration body. **The ticket is checked for ownership**, so one teacher cannot complete another's upload into their own scope.

Writable by staff within the same branch scope an upload takes (§4.9): a Teacher may **read** Global content and may not **edit** it. Out-of-scope answers **404, never 403** (§20 rule 17).

get.description: TD-3.5, TD-12, §4.9, §3.1, §20 rule 4. **The only way private content is ever read.** Private-bucket objects are never exposed through stable URLs; every read is a short-lived presigned GET minted **after** a server-side permission check. **Three rules meet here.** (1) **TD-12 freshness** — *"statelessness ends where safeguarding begins"*: an unexpired access token is not sufficient, so `account_status` and the role assignment are re-read from the database on **every** request, and a Teacher suspended mid-session loses access to a private recording **at once** rather than at token expiry. (2) **The §4.9 tiers**, applied through the **same predicate `GET /library` uses** and deliberately not a second expression of it — the rule that decides what a person may see in a list is the rule that decides what they may open. (3) **Child context** (§4.3) for a Parent acting on a minor's behalf: `X-Active-Child-ID` is verified against an approved `FamilyLink` on this very request, and the private-tier check is narrowed to **that** child. The middleware is not mounted on the route, because staff reach content by a different path and would be asked for a header they have no reason to send. **TTL 10 minutes** (TD-12), and the response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` — a shared cache would hand one caller's grant to another. Out-of-scope content answers **404, never 403** (§20 rule 17), so a response cannot confirm a file exists.

Omitting it on an edit **leaves the tier alone**. **The tier does NOT gate this management list** — role and branch scope do, as before; a tier that hid a sitting from the Admin who must un-hide it would make it unadministrable rather than confidential.

post.description: TD-3.6 (R58), §4.6. **A physical sitting**: `{ mode, title, max_grade, description?, date, start_time, end_time, level_id, subject_id, academic_year_id, branch_id, room_id, administrative_group_id?, visibility?, staff[] }`. **`mode` accepts `physical` and `online`, and `online` is REFUSED** with `409 STATE_CONFLICT` and `details.reason = ONLINE_NOT_AVAILABLE` — the interface offers it disabled (§14.4) and the schema names it, so a client learns *which* capability is missing rather than receiving a generic validation error. **No online endpoint exists**, deliberately: a route with nothing behind it appears in the contract as a capability that exists. **R58 supersedes §4.6's "digital exams only in MVP"**: a sitting is organised here — branch, room, date, clock window and staff — while the **paper** (questions, print layout, marking) stays outside the platform. Times are TD-11 **wall-clock**, never instants. The place fields are **required here** though the columns are nullable: §7's standing division, nullable for rows predating the requirement and required where a person is asked. **The Level/Subject pairing goes through the shared curriculum policy** — the same assertion scheduling, teaching-group splits and content use, so `SUBJECT_NOT_IN_LEVEL` means the same thing on all four. A room must belong to the chosen branch (`ROOM_BRANCH_MISMATCH`, the name sessions already use), and a narrower `administrative_group_id` must be a roster of that Level at that branch (`BRANCH_MISMATCH` / `GROUP_LEVEL_MISMATCH`), or the exam would be sat by people it was not written for. **Each refusal reuses the code the platform already gives that rule** — a second spelling is how a client ends up showing the wrong remedy. **Staff are supervisors, not instructors** — one `supervisor` and any number of `assistant`s, the shape `CourseScheduleStaff` already uses. **R109 — `visibility`.** `public` (the default, and what every sitting before this revision was) | `private` | `hidden`, superseding §4.6's *an exam has no visibility tier of its own* — that clause described the **audience** and answered nothing about whether the arrangement is announced. One column and no snapshot: a sitting materializes nothing. `hidden` is read by its `ExamStaff.position = 'supervisor'` and by Super Admins, and by nobody else. Omitting it on an edit **leaves the tier alone**. **The tier does NOT gate this management list** — role and branch scope do, as before; a tier that hid a sitting from the Admin who must un-hide it would make it unadministrable rather than confidential.

patch.description: TD-3.6 (R58). **The arrangements are editable; the identity is not.** `title`, `description`, `date`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `room_id`, `administrative_group_id` and `staff` may change — those are arrangements, and arrangements change. **`mode`, `level_id`, `subject_id`, `academic_year_id` and `branch_id` are refused** by a `.strict()` schema rather than dropped: each would change *what is examined, for whom, or where* while keeping the grades and submissions already recorded against the old answer, which is the reasoning §4.4 applies to a course schedule's scope. Moving an exam to another level is a new exam. **TD-15**: a stale `version` is `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`, never a silent overwrite. **Staff are REPLACED, not merged** — one call is one decision, and there is no window in which the exam holds half of an intended change. **R109 — `visibility`.** `public` (the default, and what every sitting before this revision was) | `private` | `hidden`, superseding §4.6's *an exam has no visibility tier of its own* — that clause described the **audience** and answered nothing about whether the arrangement is announced. One column and no snapshot: a sitting materializes nothing. `hidden` is read by its `ExamStaff.position = 'supervisor'` and by Super Admins, and by nobody else. Omitting it on an edit **leaves the tier alone**. **The tier does NOT gate this management list** — role and branch scope do, as before; a tier that hid a sitting from the Admin who must un-hide it would make it unadministrable rather than confidential.

The ninety-day window then applies as it does to every other entity.
